system_overview: This specification models a simple sequential algorithm that finds the largest value in a sequence of natural numbers by scanning from left to right. Its primary purpose is educational: it serves as an exercise in defining and proving type invariants, inductive invariants, and algorithm correctness using the TLA+ proof system.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a single sequential process that iterates through a sequence. There are no concurrent actors or distributed components.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) an input sequence of natural numbers that does not change during execution, (2) the current highest value seen so far (initialized to negative one to handle the case of an empty sequence), (3) a loop index tracking the current position in the sequence, and (4) a program counter indicating whether the algorithm is still looping or has finished.
initial_state: The input sequence is drawn nondeterministically from the set of all finite sequences of natural numbers. The highest-seen value is negative one. The loop index starts at one (the first position). The program counter indicates the loop has not yet completed.
actions: There are two actions: (1) Loop body: if the loop index has not exceeded the length of the sequence, the algorithm compares the element at the current index with the current highest value, keeps whichever is larger, and advances the index by one. If the index exceeds the sequence length, the algorithm transitions to a done state. (2) Termination stuttering: once the algorithm has completed, the system stutters (no state change) to prevent deadlock.
safety_properties: Type correctness: the input sequence is always a sequence of natural numbers, the loop index is always between one and the length of the sequence plus one, the loop index is always a natural number, and the highest-seen value is always a natural number or negative one. Inductive invariant: at every point during execution, every element of the sequence at positions before the current loop index is less than or equal to the current highest-seen value. Correctness: after the algorithm terminates, the highest-seen value is greater than or equal to every element in the entire input sequence. When the algorithm finishes, the loop index equals the length of the sequence plus one.
liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches the done state.
additional_assumptions: The specification is written using PlusCal syntax which is translated to TLA+. The specification includes formal hierarchical proofs of: (1) the type invariant, (2) the inductive invariant (using the type invariant as a lemma), (3) a helper theorem that the loop index equals sequence length plus one upon completion, and (4) overall correctness (derived from the preceding invariants). The max function used returns the first argument when both are equal.
